points.why: It covers consistent answers (fixed query tools) and frequent change (automatic freshness), but never argues a graph is justified over a diagram, and even suggests a Postgres CTE would do.

It chooses by how the facts are described: properties sit naturally on edges in Neo4j, RDF is strong on standards and federation, and preference alone is rejected as a reason; Neptune is not mentioned.
It says reachability is a lookup the graph answers, while the cascade needs a separate dynamic simulator, and it names retry amplification as a reinforcing feedback loop.
It recommends provenance, declared vs observed edges, and checking answers against incidents, but not verifying dependency facts the agent extracted itself.
